Artistic Dental Lab, Bangalore — my dental laboratory in India. One of three businesses running alongside aaoms in India and aaoms in Nepal.

Ventures I run: Artistic Dental Lab, Bangalore — dental laboratory work in India. aaoms.co.in — premium medical and uniform wear for India, based in Bangalore. aaomsnepal.com — medical wear and embroidery for Nepal, based at Mahendra Nagar, Dhanusha. aaomsDigital — software, websites, AI video, advertising, 3D and embroidery digitizing, plus the aaomsPrint card printing engine. Freelance 3D animation for clients including Cora CGI and Accenture. Own pipeline, own standards, delivered remotely.
Creative Head at Dubai Times, Dubai — leading the creative side: direction, output standards and the team behind them.

Career: started on the studio floor at Motion Picture, Bangalore — modelling, animation and the discipline of a delivery date. Then Creative Head at Dubai Times, Dubai, leading direction and output standards. After that, freelance 3D animation for clients including Cora CGI and Accenture. About ten years in production altogether. Running my own ventures now, and open to the right role if the offer is strong.
Blockchain is specialized infrastructure. Use it when multiple parties need shared truth without a single operator — not as a default database.
CRM tracks relationships and follow-ups. A simple disciplined pipeline beats a complex empty one.
ERP ties inventory, orders, accounting. Only adopt modules you’ll actually operate daily.
Ecommerce needs catalog, cart, payment, fulfillment, and support. aaomsnepal.com / aaoms.co.in are live storefronts in that family.
SEO: clear pages, fast loads, honest titles, real content. Shops benefit from structured product data.
UI is what you see; UX is whether the job gets done without friction. Measure tasks completed, not opinions only.
Scrum is one way to cadence work. If velocity theater replaces user value, simplify.
Agile works when feedback is real and scope is honest. Ceremonies without delivery are just calendar tax.
Networking: DNS, HTTP, TLS, firewalls. Most ‘app bugs’ are still misconfigured paths and certificates.
Linux is the default server OS for most web stacks. Learn shell basics — it compounds forever.
Git is version control. Small commits, clear messages, and branches that match reality save teams.
JOINs combine related tables. Start from the question you need answered, then shape the query.
CSS is layout and visual system. Design tokens and restraint beat random restyling.
HTML structures web content. Keep it semantic; accessibility is part of quality, not a polish phase.
Express is a minimal Node framework for HTTP APIs and static sites — simple and widely deployed.
Node.js powers JavaScript on the server — APIs, terminals, and lightweight services (this site uses Express/Node).
React is a UI library for component-based frontends. Fine default for interactive dashboards and shop admin screens.
TypeScript adds types to JavaScript so larger apps break earlier in the editor, not only in production.
JavaScript/TypeScript runs the web UI and many Node backends — including tools like this site’s server.
Python is a top language for automation, data work, and backends. Great first tool for scripts around shops and ops.

aaomsDigital / aaomsTech angle: storefronts, terminals, print-queue tools, automation scripts, and production-minded software. For broader IT solutions — cloud, web apps, integrations — describe your stack and goal; contact hello@kkpramod.com.np or WhatsApp +9779803840868.

IT sector spans software products, services, SaaS, infrastructure, data, and cybersecurity. Nepal’s scene is growing around outsourcing, startups, and local digital products; India is a global delivery and product hub. This shell sits on the craft + commerce side: aaoms shops, Evolis print systems, and production software.

Software development here means practical shipping: web apps, Node/API tools, shop systems, terminals, and automation around aaomsDigital. Good engineering = clear requirements, clean interfaces, reliable deploys. Stack examples: JavaScript/Node, modern frontends, APIs, and print/ops tooling.

Data science: collect → clean → model → decide. Useful skills: Python, SQL, statistics, visualization, and careful validation. For business, start with the decision you need — not the fanciest model. This terminal itself is a lightweight knowledge agent, not a full ML platform.
Cloud & DevOps: deploy reliably, observe, and iterate. Containers, CI/CD, and managed databases remove a lot of ops pain when used simply. Pick boring technology until scale forces complexity.
Security basics that matter: least privilege, updates, backups, MFA, and not pasting secrets into chat. Treat production credentials like production fabric stock — controlled and tracked.

Databases: use relational (SQL) when structure and transactions matter; document/key-value stores when flexibility or speed of iteration dominates. Model data around real queries, not textbook purity.
Frontend = what users touch. Backend = rules, data, integrations. APIs connect them. Prefer clear REST/JSON unless you have a real GraphQL need. Ship small, measure, improve.

aaoms Nepal uses comfort-first fabrics for medical and everyday wear: soft recovery blends, breathable weaves, and 4-way stretch options on premium lines. Pipeline: design → fabric select → cut → sew → embroidery (optional) → finish → QC → ship. Warehouse: Bateshwor, Mahendra Nagar, Dhanusha, Nepal. Shop: aaomsnepal.com

Premium stretch lines use 4-way stretch comfort fabrics aimed at all-shift movement — soft recovery, shape hold, and durable wear. See stretch / premium collections on aaomsnepal.com.

aaomsPrint runs on Evolis Primacy / Primacy 2 class direct-to-card printers.
• Format: CR-80 (85.6 × 53.98 mm ISO)
• Design target: 1011 × 638 px @ 300 dpi
• Tech: dye-sublimation / resin thermal transfer, edge-to-edge
• Features: photo, QR/barcode, dual-side, encoding-ready
• Workflow: design → queue → print inside aaomsDigital

aaomsPrint standard: CR-80 ISO card 85.6 × 53.98 mm · 1011 × 638 pixels at 300 dpi · edge-to-edge. Hardware: Evolis Primacy-class. Typical single-sided color ~190–225 cards/hour depending on ribbon and encoding.

• Terrain: Himalaya (north), hills, Terai plains (south)
• 77 districts · 7 provinces · federal democratic republic
• Currency: Nepalese Rupee (NPR) · Time: UTC+5:45

India storefront: https://aaoms.co.in — premium medical wear & embroidery in ₹. Main focus of this shell is aaomsnepal.com and Nepal operations.

Nepal is a federal democratic republic (since 2008, monarchy abolished). Multi-party system, coalition governments common. Constitution 2015. Politics can be lively — parties, protests, and power-sharing are part of the landscape. For India: world's largest democracy, parliamentary system, regular national and state elections. Ask a more specific angle if you want deeper context.

NEPSE is the Nepal Stock Exchange — the only stock exchange of Nepal, based in Kathmandu. It trades banks, hydropower, insurance, manufacturing and more. You can see live gainers, losers, momentum systems and technical indicators on this site at /nepse (NEPSE Screener). Educational use only — not investment advice.

Open the free NEPSE Screener on this site: /nepse. It shows live session data, top gainers & losers, and five screen types (Darvas-style breakouts, momentum, consolidation, volume, weakness). It also has technical indicators (MACD, RSI, Supertrend, Bollinger, ADX, ATR, Stochastic and more) plus momentum systems (TSM, Dual, Donchian, MACD, RSI Trend). Purely educational.

India has two main exchanges: NSE (National Stock Exchange) and BSE (Bombay Stock Exchange). Key indices are Nifty 50 (NSE) and Sensex (BSE). They are among the largest and most liquid markets in Asia. Many Nepali investors also follow Nifty and Sensex because of the close economic links. This site focuses on NEPSE tools; for Indian live data use official NSE/BSE or apps like Groww, Zerodha, or Moneycontrol.

Major world markets: US (S&P 500, Nasdaq, Dow Jones), Europe (FTSE 100, DAX, CAC 40), Asia (Nikkei, Hang Seng, Shanghai, Nifty, NEPSE). US markets often set the global tone. When US futures or overnight moves are strong, Asian markets including NEPSE and Nifty can react the next day. Always treat global data as context, not as a direct signal for Nepal or India stocks.

For Nepal: use the NEPSE Screener on this site → /nepse (live gainers, losers, screens and indicators). For India: Nifty 50 & Sensex via NSE/BSE official sites or apps. For world markets: S&P 500, Nasdaq, Dow. Remember — this terminal and the /nepse page are educational only. Never treat any answer here as buy/sell advice.

NEPSE regular trading hours are typically Sunday to Thursday, 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM Nepal Time (with a pre-open session). Exact times can change on special days — always confirm on the official NEPSE website or the status shown on /nepse.
NSE and BSE regular equity market hours are Monday to Friday, 9:15 AM to 3:30 PM Indian Standard Time. Pre-open is earlier. Indian markets are closed on weekends and national holidays.

US equity markets (NYSE, Nasdaq) regular hours are Monday–Friday 9:30 AM to 4:00 PM Eastern Time. That is evening/night in Nepal. Futures trade almost 24 hours and often influence the next Asian session.

Open the free Price Action Classroom on this site: /classroom (also /learn or /price-action). It is an online slide classroom — Darvas-style thinking, funny candle names, stop-loss rules, risk control, and classic patterns. Educational only. No download — read online or take screenshots.

Sniper-style rules taught in the Classroom: divide capital into 10 parts, stay alert on live setups, execute quickly or wait for the next trade, respect stop-loss on daily close basis, keep discipline + patience. Without discipline and patience, every fancy pattern is garbage. See /classroom.

Darvas idea: buy strength. A box forms, then breakout, then retest often gives a second chance. The classic quote: the only sound reason for buying a stock is that it is rising in price. Learn the box + checklist in the Price Action Classroom → /classroom. Educational only.

Classroom buying filter: near or at all-time high, less talked about, low float, superb quarterly numbers, bright future potential. Still not a buy tip — only a filter for study. Full slides at /classroom.

Simple stop-loss style from the Classroom: 5 EMA for very short-term, 10 EMA for swing, 20 EMA for positional, 200 EMA for investors (exit if price closes below on daily). Respect the stop on daily close basis. Details at /classroom.

Funny candle names used for memory in the Classroom: Chikni Chameli (clean strong bullish), Lal Dabangg (big red seller control), Chudail (ugly rejection/trap), Lollipop (long wick small body), Chotu Chotu Baby (tiny candles after a move — base building). Names help memory; structure still decides. See /classroom.

Classroom covers patterns such as High Dry Fry (sharp up → correction → baby-candle base → next leg), Baap–Beta style follow-through, Inside Bar, 123 pattern, Morning Star, Bullish Tasuki, Rising Three, Double Bottom. Open /classroom for the full slide set. Educational only — not signals.

Iron Triangle of risk (Classroom): A = max money you may risk on the trade (often ≤ 2% of account), B = distance from entry to stop per share, C = A ÷ B = maximum shares. Never risk more than your plan allows. Learn it at /classroom.

Common Fib pullback levels taught in the Classroom: 23.6%, 38.2% (strong trend), 50%, 61.8% golden ratio. Many swings struggle in deeper retracement zones. Combine with structure, not Fib alone. See /classroom.

Why many prefer equity cash (Classroom): no leverage, less gap fear than F&O, no forced expiry, strong names can bounce, you need not stare at the screen all day, fewer but more meaningful trades. Swing/positional with GTT can fit a normal job. Details at /classroom.

Classroom rule: never average a stock that is going down — it goes against strength-based Darvas-style thinking. Cut or respect the stop instead. Educational mindset, not a personal order. More at /classroom.
